oneOf.description:
Removes a green or blue screen from a raster, in linear light.

Each pixel's chromaticity, its colour divided by its brightness, is compared with the key
color's, so a screen keys evenly from its shadows to its highlights. Pixels within
`tolerance` of the key are removed, kept in full beyond `tolerance + softness`, and fade
between. Near-black pixels have no reliable hue and are always kept. Then `spill` pulls the
key's dominant channel down to the larger of the other two on the pixels that remain, which
takes the green or blue cast out of edges and reflections. The result keeps the source's
alpha times the matte. With `matte_only`, the output is white with that alpha instead, which
can feed `merge`'s mask or `channels`.

For example, `{ "key_color": [0, 177, 64, 255], "tolerance": 0.1, "softness": 0.1 }` on
footage shot against a green screen leaves the subject over transparency.

oneOf.description:
Corrects the colour of a raster. Each step works on the straight colour in linear light, in
this order, and the alpha is untouched, so the defaults leave the raster unchanged.

1. White balance multiplies red, green and blue by `2^(temperature / 2)`, `2^(-tint / 2)` and
`2^(-temperature / 2)`, divided by the Rec. 709 luminance of those three, so a neutral grey
keeps its brightness.

2. Lift, gain and offset: `gain * (x + lift * (1 - x)) + offset` on each channel.

3. Gamma: `max(x, 0) ^ (1 / gamma)` on each channel.

4. Contrast: `pivot * (max(x, 0) / pivot) ^ contrast` on each channel.

5. Curves act on the sRGB-encoded colour, clamped to 0..1: `master` on every channel, then
`red`, `green` and `blue` on theirs. Each is a smooth monotone curve through its points, flat
before the first and after the last. With no curves set, values above 1 pass through.

Each channel param is `[red, green, blue]`; an expression for one is a `vec3`. A curve is up
to 16 `[x, y]` points of numbers or expressions, with `x` increasing, all in 0..1:
`"curves": { "master": [[0, 0], [0.5, 0.65], [1, 1]] }` brightens the midtones.

contrast.title: Contrast

curves.title: Curves

oneOf.description:
Pins a raster's four corners to four points of the canvas, with the perspective that takes.

`top_left`, `top_right`, `bottom_right` and `bottom_left` are where the source's own corners
land, in canvas pixels, which run clockwise on screen from the top left when the source is
pinned upright. The source is stretched across the quad they make, with perspective, and the
canvas outside the quad is transparent. The corners can't default to the source's own, so
they default to a 100 pixel square at the canvas's top left; set all four.

The corners must make a convex quad with some area. Corners that cross each other, bend a
corner inwards or lie in a line fail the render, naming the corner at fault when it can. Run
the other way round, the corners mirror the source. They are checked at every frame, so
animated corners must stay convex throughout.

The quad's edges are antialiased, and the source is filtered for how much the pin shrinks it
at each pixel, so the far end of a steep pin does not alias. With `motion_blur`, animated
corners smear along their motion.

For example, pinning a 1920 by 1080 video onto a tilted screen in a plate:
`{ "top_left": [412, 210], "top_right": [905, 262], "bottom_right": [893, 540], "bottom_left": [405, 498] }`.

oneOf.description:
Grows or shrinks the opaque part of a raster by `radius` pixels, for pulling a key's edge in,
widening a matte so a blur covers the whole object, or outlining a letter that is already
pixels.

A pixel counts as part of the shape when its alpha is at least 0.5. A positive `radius` makes
every pixel within that distance of the shape opaque, in the colour of the nearest pixel of the
shape, so the result composites without a dark fringe. A negative `radius` makes every pixel
within that distance of transparency, or of an edge of the raster's area that is not an edge of
the canvas, transparent, and keeps the colour of the pixels that remain. Alpha is never
lowered by growing nor raised by shrinking, and `softness` fades the new edge over that many
pixels. Growing widens the output past the source's area by the radius; shrinking keeps the
source's area. With `radius` and `softness` 0, the raster is unchanged.

For example, `radius` 3 grows a key's matte by 3 pixels, and merging the original over a
`radius` 4 result outlines a rasterized letter.

oneOf.description:
A 2D outline, a `path_2d`, `shape_2d` or `text_2d` wired into `geometry`, extruded into a solid:
a front cap facing +Z, a back cap facing -Z and side walls, lit, single-sided and white unless a
`material_3d` is wired into `material`. A `material_3d` wired into `side_material` covers the
side walls and the bevel instead, leaving the caps to `material`. The geometry's pixel coordinates, after its own
position, scale, rotation and anchor, become world X and Y at `units_per_pixel` units each, with
Y flipped, since 2D Y points down and 3D Y up. Pixel (0, 0) is the origin that `placement`
moves and turns the solid about, and nothing re-centres the solid on it: the geometry's
`position` and `anchor` decide where it sits about that origin, so a `shape_2d` at `position`
(0, 0) lies to the right of and below it on screen, and 100 pixels across it is 1 unit wide.
The extrusion is centred on Z = 0. The outline is filled by the nonzero rule, as a `text_3d`
glyph is, so holes of a path stay open whichever way they wind and overlapping subpaths join;
open subpaths are closed by a straight segment. Curves are flattened to within 0.001 world
units, so a larger or smaller `units_per_pixel` keeps them as smooth. An ellipse has as many
sides as that takes, at least 16 and at most 256, and each corner of a rounded rectangle a
quarter of as many for its own radius, at least 4 and at most 64. The flattening of a path or
a text coarsens where it would pass 16384 points. A solid takes at most 256 contours, 16384 points,
262144 vertices and 786432 indices, and bevels fit outlines of at most 4096 points; more is a
render error. An `offset_2d` in the geometry is not supported yet and fails the render. The
mesh is built again only when the outline, `units_per_pixel` or the bevel change, or the
`depth` of a bevelled one, so animating the placement, the material or a plain extrusion's
depth costs no more than for a `shape_3d`.

the bevel it gets the widest one that fits.

oneOf.description:
Adds film grain to a raster: noise that follows the picture's brightness, in a pattern fixed to
the canvas, so it stays put as the source moves and looks the same at any render scale. Alpha
is untouched. Set `seed` to `"=frame"` for grain that changes every frame, as in
`{ "amount": 0.1, "size": 2, "seed": "=frame" }`.

amount.description:
Grain strength: the standard deviation of the grain in sRGB-encoded units, at the
brightness where `response` makes it strongest.
amount.title: Amount

monochrome.description: Uses one grain for all channels, which adds no colour noise, rather than one per channel.
monochrome.title: Monochrome

response.description:
How much the strength follows the brightness. 0 grains every brightness alike, and 1
grains midtones only, leaving black and white clean.
response.title: Response

roughness.description:
Mixes in a coarser grain four times the size, for a paper-like tooth, without changing the
strength. 0 is fine grain only and 1 coarse grain only.

seed.description: Picks an unrelated pattern. Use an expression such as `=frame` to animate the grain.

brightest channel, so dark pixels add nothing.

up from black to white as they look. Brighter pixels glow more, white at full strength,
and 1 lets nothing glow. Past 254/255 white dims too, so the glow fades out
continuously as the threshold reaches 1.

be a solid color; a gradient is an error.

oneOf.description:
Redraws a raster as a grid of dots or lines in `ink` on `paper`, as in a print screen. Each
cell takes the darkness, 1 minus the luma of the sRGB-encoded colour, at its centre, and
covers that fraction of its area, so a flat colour gives uniform dots and black fills the
whole cell. The grid is anchored to the canvas origin, so the pattern stays put when the
source moves, and the source's alpha is kept.

For example, `{ "pitch": 55, "angle": -19, "ink": [110, 28, 38, 255], "paper": [120, 134, 150, 255] }`
over a flat colour gives oxblood dots on a grey-blue ground, on a grid rotated -19 degrees.

angle.description: Rotation of the grid in degrees.
angle.title: Angle

ink.description: Color where the source is dark. Must be a solid color; a gradient is an error.
ink.title: Ink

paper.description: Color where the source is light. Must be a solid color; a gradient is an error.
paper.title: Paper

pitch.description: Width and height of a cell in pixels.
pitch.title: Pitch

oneOf.title: Halftone

oneOf.description: Adjusts raster hue, saturation, and lightness of the sRGB-encoded colour.
oneOf.title: Hue Saturation

oneOf.description:
Shows a raster, such as text or video, on a flat rectangle facing +Z. With no `material_3d`
wired into `material` it is unlit and double-sided, so it looks as it does in 2D while it faces
the camera. A `material_3d` applies exactly as it is set, so a default one makes the plane lit
and single-sided; set its `unlit` and `double_sided` to keep the plane as it looks unwired.
A plane is drawn blended, ordered by its centre among blended objects, so its transparent parts
show what is behind it. Planes that intersect, or overlap while crossing in depth, can show in
the wrong order; layers separated in depth, and opaque shapes in front of or behind planes, are
ordered correctly. `opaque` draws a plane that has no transparent pixels with the opaque
objects instead. A source keeps its detail when it is shown at its own size or larger; shown
smaller, it is filtered with mipmaps, trilinearly and anisotropically, before `render_3d`'s
`supersample` averages it, unless `sampling` is `nearest`.

matte.description:
The matte its visible coverage goes to, by a name `render_3d`'s `mattes` lists, for that
render's `matte` output. Empty takes the matte of the nearest `merge_3d`, `instance_3d` or
`particles_3d` holding it that names one, or none.
matte.title: Matte

opaque.description:
Draws the plane with the opaque objects, writing depth, rather than blended. For a source
with no transparent pixels, this orders the plane correctly against any geometry it
intersects or crosses in depth. Alpha is then ignored: the colour's alpha, `opacity` and the
source's alpha. A source pixel that is transparent shows its colour at full opacity, which
is black for a fully transparent one, and a half-transparent one shows its colour
undimmed. It casts a shadow over its whole rectangle. A shadow catcher is always drawn as
one, so this has no effect on it.
opaque.title: Opaque

position.description: Position in world units along X, Y and Z, in the parent's space.
position.title: Position

region.description:
Shows only this part of the source, `[x, y, width, height]` in the source's pixels from its
top left, on a plane that covers just that part, so a plane showing a region is where it
would be and as big as it would be with the whole source on it: it looks as a plane
showing a `crop` of that region does, where `width` is still the width of the whole
source, and `position`, `rotation` and `scale` pivot about the whole source's centre.
Cut off at the source's edges as `crop` cuts its region, and a region with no pixel
left shows nothing. Each of the four numbers takes an integer or an expression, which is
truncated toward zero as `crop`'s are; the whole region cannot be an expression. Unset
shows the whole source. Planes showing parts of one source share its texture and mip
levels and draw together, so a region costs nothing beyond the plane, where a `crop`
costs a raster the size of the source and a draw of its own. Sampling is kept inside the
region, so what is outside it isn't meant to show. To keep it so under strong minification,
the band along each edge of the region that is inside the source, and all of a narrow
region, is sampled from a sharper mip level than its footprint, since a texel of a shared
level can hold pixels from both sides of the edge: it can alias or shimmer there where a
`crop` would be smooth, across the whole of a piece drawn much smaller than its pixels.
region.title: Region

rotation.description:
Rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z, applied as yaw about Y, then pitch about the turned
X, then roll about the turned Z.
rotation.title: Rotation

sampling.description:
`nearest` gives each pixel the one source texel under it at any size, for pixel art:
magnified, texels stay hard-edged squares; shown smaller, a pixel picks one texel instead
of averaging the ones it covers, so it aliases and shimmers where `linear` is smooth.
`render_3d`'s `supersample` still averages its samples within each pixel.
sampling.title: Sampling

scale.description: Scale multiplier along X, Y and Z, applied before the rotation.
scale.title: Scale

width.description:
Width in world units, 1 being as wide as a default `shape_3d` box; the height follows the
aspect ratio of the source's full display size.
width.title: Width

oneOf.title: Image Plane 3D

oneOf.description:
Draws its input scene `count` times, each copy placed by `position`, `rotation` and `scale`
evaluated for that copy, where `instance` is the copy's index from 0 and `instance_count` is
`count`: `position = vec3((instance % 10) * 1.5, 0, floor(instance / 10) * 1.5)` lays out a
grid, and a ring, a spiral or a path follow from `sin`, `cos` and `path_point` of
`instance / instance_count`. A copy is placed in the input scene's own space, so it turns and
scales about the origin of the scene's own coordinates.

`tint` colours each copy: `tint = rgb(255 * instance / instance_count, 128, 255)` shifts the
colour along the copies, and it multiplies the objects' base colours and emissive light, so
copies of a white or textured object take the tint's colour. Its alpha is ignored.

Copies placed by hand are listed in `copies` instead, as literals: `copies = [{ "position":
[0, 0, 0], "scale": [1, 2, 1], "tint": "#ff8040" }, { "position": [2, 0, 1], "rotation":
[0, 45, 0] }]` places two. `count`, `position`, `rotation`, `scale` and `tint` must not be set
beside a `copies` list that has copies, or `check` fails. A list is placed once, so a frame
after the first does no work per copy.

Copies share the input's meshes, textures, materials and joint matrices on the GPU, so every
copy of a skinned model plays the same animation at the same time. Opaque surfaces draw all
their copies at once from placements and tints kept on the GPU, so a moving camera or parent
costs nothing per copy, and neither does a frame when the params don't read the frame. Blended
surfaces, and those showing a raster, are copied one by one, which costs more. Only the objects
are copied: the input's lights and camera appear once, placed as they would be without the node,
so copies don't multiply a scene's lighting. Shadows, fog and the environment treat a copy as any
other object. An `instance_3d` may hold another, which multiplies their counts, up to 8 deep.
A scene draws at most 100000 objects in all, counting each copy's objects, and a count that
would exceed this fails the render. The node is static when its params don't read the frame
and its scene is static.

copies.description:
Copies to place, each given literally as `{ position, rotation, scale, tint }` with any
field left out taking the default of the param of that name: position and rotation 0,
scale 1 and a white tint. The list can't hold expressions and holds at most 100000
copies. An empty list places none of its own. When it has copies, `count`, `position`,
`rotation`, `scale` and `tint` must not be set, and `check` fails if they are.
copies.title: Copies

count.description:
Copies to place, from 0 to 100000. 0 leaves the node's scene out entirely, lights and
cameras too. Not set together with `copies`.
count.title: Count

matte.description:
The matte, by a name `render_3d`'s `mattes` lists, of every object inside it that names
none of its own, for that render's `matte` output. Empty passes on the matte of the
nearest `merge_3d`, `instance_3d` or `particles_3d` holding it that names one, or none.
matte.title: Matte

position.description: Position in world units along X, Y and Z of each copy, in the scene's own space. Evaluated for every copy, and can read `instance` and `instance_count`.
position.title: Position

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z of each copy, applied as yaw about Y, then pitch about the turned X, then roll about the turned Z. Evaluated for every copy, and can read `instance` and `instance_count`.
rotation.title: Rotation

scale.description: Scale multiplier along X, Y and Z of each copy, applied before the rotation. Evaluated for every copy, and can read `instance` and `instance_count`.
scale.title: Scale

tint.description:
Colour that multiplies the base colour of every object in each copy, texture and base
colour map included, and the light they give off, so a glowing copy glows in its tint.
White leaves a copy as it is. Evaluated for every copy, and can read `instance` and
`instance_count`. Its alpha is ignored: a copy is opaque or blended exactly as its
material makes it. Tints of nested `instance_3d` nodes multiply. Must be a solid color; a
gradient fails `check`.
tint.title: Tint

oneOf.title: Instance 3D

oneOf.description:
A 2D profile, a `path_2d`, `shape_2d` or `text_2d` wired into `geometry`, spun around the world Y axis
into a solid of revolution, lit, single-sided and white unless a `material_3d` is wired into
`material`. The geometry's pixel coordinates, after its own position, scale, rotation and
anchor, become world units at `units_per_pixel` each: a point's X is its distance from the axis
and its Y, flipped since 2D Y points down and 3D Y up, its height, so pixel (0, 0) is on the
axis at height 0, which is the origin that `placement` moves and turns the solid about. Points
left of the axis are put on it. Each contour becomes a strip of quads around the axis, shaded
smoothly around it, and along the profile except at corners sharper than 30°, which stay hard.
A closed contour makes a closed ring solid whose faces point out of the area it encloses,
whichever way it winds. An open contour makes a surface whose front faces the right-hand side of
the direction it is drawn in, and which is seen from both sides only if its material is
`double_sided`. A point on the axis is a pole, where the surface closes to a point, such as the
tip of a cone or the top of a dome; the quads there are triangles, so no triangle without
area is left in the mesh, and a closed contour's edge along the axis draws nothing. Contours
are spun separately, so one inside another is a separate solid and not a hole. A solid takes
at most 256 contours, 16384 profile points, 262144 vertices and 786432 indices in all, which
is the profile's vertices times the steps around; more is a render error. The mesh is built
again only when the profile, `units_per_pixel`, `segments` or `sweep` change, so animating the
placement or the material costs no more than for a `shape_3d`.

matte.description:
The matte its visible coverage goes to, by a name `render_3d`'s `mattes` lists, for that
render's `matte` output. Empty takes the matte of the nearest `merge_3d`, `instance_3d` or
`particles_3d` holding it that names one, or none.
matte.title: Matte

position.title: Position

rotation.description:
Rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z, applied as yaw about Y, then pitch about the turned
X, then roll about the turned Z.
rotation.title: Rotation

scale.description: Scale multiplier along X, Y and Z, applied before the rotation.
scale.title: Scale

segments.description:
Steps around the axis for a whole turn, from 3 to 512; a `sweep` of less than 360° has
proportionally fewer. The surface is shaded smoothly around the axis, so a few dozen look
round.
segments.title: Segments

sweep.description:
How far around the axis the profile turns, in degrees, from 0 to 360, starting on +X and
turning towards -Z. Under 360 leaves an open wedge with no end caps; 0 draws nothing.
sweep.title: Sweep

World units that one pixel of the geometry spans, so that at the default of 0.01 a
100 pixel profile is 1 unit across. The geometry's own position, scale and rotation apply
before it. 0 draws nothing. At most 1000000.
units_per_pixel.title: Units Per Pixel

oneOf.title: Lathe 3D

oneOf.description:
Blurs a raster as an out-of-focus lens does: every point spreads into an evenly lit disc, or a
polygon with `blades`, so highlights turn into bokeh rather than the soft glow of `blur`.

Without `depth`, everything blurs by `radius`. With it, each pixel blurs by its depth: sharp
within `focus_range` of `focus`, and more so further away, up to `radius`. Depth is the red
channel of `depth`, read where each pixel is, and 0 where it stores nothing, so a
`render_3d`'s `depth` output gives depth of field and any greyscale raster works, as a
gradient that is dark in a band across the frame gives tilt-shift. `focus` is in that 0 to 1
range, not in world units. A blurred pixel nearer than its neighbours spreads over them even
where they are sharp, and one further away doesn't spread over nearer, sharper pixels, so a
sharp subject keeps its edges in front of a blurred background.

An optional `mask` keeps pieces sharp: where it is 1 a pixel stays as it is and doesn't spread
over its neighbours, where it is 0 the blur is as above, and in between the blur shrinks by
that share. `mask_mode` picks the channel read, as `merge`'s does, and `mask` reads 0 where it
stores nothing. Pairing a `render_3d`'s `depth` with one of its `matte` channels defocuses a
scene while a piece of it, such as its lyrics, stays crisp.

The cost stays bounded at any radius: circles of more than 6 pixels are gathered from copies
of the source at half, a quarter or less of its resolution, so each pixel reads about 130
texels at most, twice that with `depth`. The widest blurs have softer bokeh edges. Blurring
widens the output past the source's area by the radius.

Defocusing a whole frame into hexagonal bokeh:

```json
{ "id": 2, "type": "lens_blur", "params": { "radius": 12, "blades": 6 }, "in": { "source": 1 } }
```

```ts
n.lens_blur({ source: photo, radius: 12, blades: 6 });
```

Depth of field from a `render_3d`, node 9, sharp at a fifth of the way from its `depth_near`
to its `depth_far`:

```json
{ "id": 10, "type": "lens_blur", "params": { "radius": 16, "focus": 0.2 } },
{ "from_node": 9, "from_port": "color", "to_node": 10, "to_port": "source" },
{ "from_node": 9, "from_port": "depth", "to_node": 10, "to_port": "depth" }
```

```ts
const { color, depth } = render.out;
n.lens_blur({ source: color, depth, radius: 16, focus: 0.2 });
```

Tilt-shift, sharp across the middle of the frame and blurred towards the top and bottom:

```json
{ "id": 2, "type": "background", "params": { "paint": { "type": "linear_gradient", "interpolation": "linear_srgb", "start": [0, 0], "end": [0, 1], "stops": [{ "offset": 0, "color": [255, 255, 255, 255] }, { "offset": 0.5, "color": [0, 0, 0, 255] }, { "offset": 1, "color": [255, 255, 255, 255] }] } } },
{ "id": 3, "type": "lens_blur", "params": { "radius": 10, "focus": 0, "focus_range": 0.1, "aperture": 1.5 }, "in": { "source": 1, "depth": 2 } }
```

The same depth of field, keeping sharp the objects of a `render_3d`'s `mattes: ["lyrics"]`,
which its `matte` output holds in its red channel:

```json
{ "id": 10, "type": "lens_blur", "params": { "radius": 16, "focus": 0.2, "mask_mode": "red" } },
{ "from_node": 9, "from_port": "color", "to_node": 10, "to_port": "source" },
{ "from_node": 9, "from_port": "depth", "to_node": 10, "to_port": "depth" },
{ "from_node": 9, "from_port": "matte", "to_node": 10, "to_port": "mask" }
```

```ts
const { color, depth, matte } = render.out;
n.lens_blur({ source: color, depth, mask: matte, radius: 16, focus: 0.2, mask_mode: "red" });
```

aperture.description:
How fast the blur grows past `focus_range`: a pixel `aperture × (|depth - focus| -
focus_range)` of the way to `radius`, up to all of it. Higher is a shallower depth of
field.
aperture.title: Aperture

blades.description:
Blades of the lens's aperture, which shape a blurred highlight: 0 is a circle, and 3 to
16 a polygon with that many sides.
blades.title: Blades

focus.description:
The depth that stays sharp, in the depth raster's 0 to 1 range. For a `render_3d`'s
`depth`, 0 is at its `depth_near` and 1 at its `depth_far`, so a distance in world units
is `(distance - depth_near) / (depth_far - depth_near)`. Unused without `depth`.
focus.title: Focus

focus_range.description: How far either side of `focus`, in the same range, depth stays sharp.
focus_range.title: Focus Range

mask_mode.description: Channel of the `mask` input that keeps pixels sharp.
mask_mode.title: Mask Mode

radius.description:
Blur radius in pixels: the blur everywhere without `depth`, and the largest blur with it.
0 leaves the source as it is. Radii above 4096 look the same.
radius.title: Radius

rotation.description: Turn of the polygon in degrees, clockwise. At 0 one corner points up.
rotation.title: Rotation

oneOf.title: Lens Blur

oneOf.description:
Bends a raster the way a lens does. With `direction: "distort"`, a pixel at `p` from the optical
centre reads the source at `p * (1 + k1 r² + k2 r⁴)`, where `r` is its distance in
half-diagonals, so positive `k1` gives barrel distortion and negative `k1` pincushion. With
`direction: "undistort"` it reads where that lens would have put it, undoing a distortion with
the same coefficients. The result covers the source's frame, and looks the same at any render
scale.

To match graphics to footage, set the footage's coefficients and `direction: "undistort"` on
the footage, or leave `direction` as `"distort"` on the graphics. For a finishing look, try
`k1: 0.15` with `chromatic_aberration: 0.004`.

center.description: The optical centre as a fraction of the frame: `[0.5, 0.5]` is the middle.
center.title: Center

chromatic_aberration.description:
How far red and blue scale apart from green, as a fraction of each pixel's distance from
the optical centre. Positive values magnify red and shrink blue, so red fringes lie
outside blue ones and grow toward the corners.
chromatic_aberration.title: Chromatic Aberration

direction.description: Whether to apply the lens or remove it.
direction.title: Direction

edge.description: What the source reads as beyond its frame.
edge.title: Edge

fit.description: Whether to scale the result so that no edge is exposed.
fit.title: Fit

k1.description:
Radial distortion, the `r²` coefficient. Positive values bow straight lines outward
(barrel), negative values bow them inward (pincushion). Distances are measured from the
optical centre in units of the frame's half-diagonal, so the corners are at 1.
k1.title: K1

k2.description: Radial distortion, the `r⁴` coefficient. It bends mostly toward the corners.
k2.title: K2

oneOf.title: Lens Distortion

oneOf.description: Remaps raster black, white, gamma, and output range of the sRGB-encoded colour.
oneOf.title: Levels

cast_shadows.description:
Casts shadows from objects that block it onto those behind them. A scene draws shadows for
its first 8 lights that cast them, in the order its scene inputs are wired, and warns
about the rest. A spot light's shadows reach 170° across at most.
cast_shadows.title: Cast Shadows

color.description: Light colour. Must be a solid color; a gradient fails `check`.
color.title: Color

intensity.description: Unitless brightness multiplier; point and spot lights fall off with the square of distance.
intensity.title: Intensity

position.description: Position in world units along X, Y and Z, in the parent's space.
position.title: Position

range.description: Distance past which a point or spot light has no effect; 0 is unlimited.
range.title: Range

rotation.description:
Rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z, applied as yaw about Y, then pitch about the turned
X, then roll about the turned Z.
rotation.title: Rotation

shadow_distance.description:
How far from the camera, along its view, a directional light's shadows reach, fading out
over the last tenth. Its shadow map spreads over what the camera sees of the scene up to
here, so a larger distance trades sharpness for reach; a scene the camera sees nearer
keeps its full sharpness.
shadow_distance.title: Shadow Distance

shadow_softness.description:
Width in world units over which shadow edges blur, up to 16 texels of the light's shadow
map, which is up to 4096 texels across and shared among the shadow-casting lights.
shadow_softness.title: Shadow Softness

spot_angle.description: Full angle of a spot light's cone in degrees.
spot_angle.title: Spot Angle

spot_softness.description: Fraction of a spot light's cone, from its edge, that fades out.
spot_softness.title: Spot Softness

oneOf.title: Light 3D

oneOf.description:
How a surface responds to light, for the 3D objects it is wired into through their `material`
input. One `material_3d` can be wired to any number of objects, which then share its params,
so changing it changes them all. Each param takes an expression as it does on any node.
Objects with no material wired in use a lit, single-sided white one; an `image_plane_3d` uses
an unlit, double-sided one. A raster wired into `texture` shows on a `shape_3d`, multiplied by
`color`, through the texture coordinates `shape_3d` describes, lit and shadowed like the rest
of the surface, and filtered as an image plane's source is unless `sampling` is `nearest`.
Its alpha counts where the material blends or masks, through `opacity` or the colour's alpha.
Wired into any other object, a material with a texture fails the render, unless it has a
`projector`; an `image_plane_3d` shows its own source and fails with either.

A scene wired into `projector` projects the `texture` from its camera, chosen as `render_3d`
would choose it, in place of texture coordinates, so it shows on any object but an image
plane, `instance_3d` copies included. Each point of the surface takes the texel the projector
sees it at: the texture fills the projector's view at the texture's own aspect ratio, with the
camera's `fov` or `ortho_height`, `near` and `far`. Faces turned away from the projector,
points outside its view and, with `projector_occlusion`, points it can't see show `color`
alone. The projector stands where its own scene places it, whatever places the objects, at the
frame being drawn, so a moving camera moves the projection: a plate projected onto geometry
wants a still `camera_3d` of its own, apart from the camera the scene is drawn from. A
`projector` without a `texture` fails the render.

`alpha_mode` `mask` draws a cut-out card, such as a `text` raster on an `image_plane_3d` whose
material is unlit and double-sided, with the opaque objects so it orders correctly where cards
cross. As a glTF `MASK` material does, it shows only the texels that reach `alpha_cutoff`.

alpha_cutoff.description: The alpha a texel needs to show when `alpha_mode` is `mask`. Not read otherwise.
alpha_cutoff.title: Alpha Cutoff

alpha_mode.description:
`blend` draws the surface blended where its alpha is below 1. `mask` draws it with the
opaque objects, so it writes depth and crossing masked surfaces order correctly: texels
whose alpha, the colour's times `opacity` times the texture's or raster's, is below
`alpha_cutoff` are discarded and the rest show at full opacity. Masked surfaces cast
shadows shaped by the cut-out. It takes precedence over `opaque` on an `image_plane_3d`,
and with `shadow_catcher` fails `check`.
alpha_mode.title: Alpha Mode

cast_shadows.description:
Blocks light from lights that cast shadows. A blended surface blocks it where its alpha is
at least half. Unlit and glowing surfaces block it too, so a shape standing in for a light,
such as a bulb around a point light, needs this off.
cast_shadows.title: Cast Shadows

color.description:
Base colour, which multiplies the `texture` on a shape and the raster on an image plane.
Must be a solid color; a gradient fails `check`.
color.title: Color

double_sided.description: Draws the back of each face too.
double_sided.title: Double Sided

emissive.description: Light the surface gives off on its own, as a multiple of its base colour.
emissive.title: Emissive

metallic.description: 0 is a dielectric such as plastic, 1 a bare metal.
metallic.title: Metallic

opacity.description:
Opacity multiplier. With `alpha_mode` `blend`, anything below 1 is drawn blended, after
opaque objects.
opacity.title: Opacity

projector_occlusion.description:
With a `projector` wired, surfaces the projector can't see, behind surfaces that cast
shadows, show the colour alone.
projector_occlusion.title: Projector Occlusion

receive_shadows.description: Darkens where shadows fall on it. An unlit surface shows them as `unlit_shadows` says.
receive_shadows.title: Receive Shadows

roughness.description: 0 is a mirror finish, 1 fully diffuse.
roughness.title: Roughness

sampling.description:
How a shape reads its `texture`, as `sampling` on `image_plane_3d`: `nearest` gives each
pixel the one texel under it at any size, for pixel art.
sampling.title: Sampling

shadow_catcher.description:
Shows nothing but the shadows falling on it, as transparent black that darkens what the
render is composited over by as much light as the shadows take away, times the colour's
alpha, the opacity and, on an image plane, its raster's alpha, whatever `unlit` says. It
shows none of its colours, hides what is behind it wherever that alpha isn't 0, and casts
no shadows, so a ground plane catching a model's shadow can stand in for the floor of 2D
footage behind it.
shadow_catcher.title: Shadow Catcher

unlit.description: Shows the base colour as is, ignoring lights.
unlit.title: Unlit

unlit_shadows.description:
How much an unlit surface darkens where shadows fall on it, from 0, which shows none, to
1, where a fully shadowed point is black. Lit surfaces ignore it, as do surfaces that
don't receive shadows.
unlit_shadows.title: Unlit Shadows

oneOf.title: Material 3D

oneOf.description: Binds an external image or video frame as a GPU texture.

alpha.description: Whether a video's colour is already multiplied by its alpha. Images ignore it.
alpha.title: Alpha

loop_mode.description: Behavior when playback leaves the source range.
loop_mode.title: Loop Mode

range_end.description: First source frame past the range; the source's end when unset.
range_end.title: Range End

source.description: External media source: a path or `media` alias, or `asset:<id>` for an asset of the host's.
source.title: Source

oneOf.title: Media In

oneOf.description:
Converts its source into the final composition output: sRGB-encoded and quantised once to the
output's format. In a template it may read a scene instead, which the clips playing the
template output.
oneOf.title: Media Output

oneOf.description: Composites an overlay raster over a base raster.

blend_mode.description:
Blend mode used when combining the overlay with the base raster. `normal` composites in
linear light; every other mode applies its formula to the sRGB-encoded colours and
composites the result in linear light.
blend_mode.title: Blend Mode

feather.description: Softens the mask edge with a Gaussian blur of this radius in pixels, applied before `invert`. Radii above about 588 look the same.
feather.title: Feather

invert.description: Swaps the masked and unmasked areas.
invert.title: Invert

mask_mode.description: Channel of the `mask` input that controls overlay visibility.
mask_mode.title: Mask Mode

oneOf.title: Merge

oneOf.description:
Draws drawings one over another in input order, the first lowest, placing them together by
its transform. The transform applies to everything inside, strokes and shadows included.

anchor.description: Pivot for scale and rotation, in pixels relative to `position`.
anchor.title: Anchor

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees, about the anchor.
rotation.title: Rotation

scale.description: Scale multiplier per axis, about the anchor.
scale.title: Scale

oneOf.title: Merge 2D

oneOf.description: Groups scenes into one, placed together by its transform.

matte.description:
The matte, by a name `render_3d`'s `mattes` lists, of every object inside it that names
none of its own, for that render's `matte` output. Empty passes on the matte of the
nearest `merge_3d`, `instance_3d` or `particles_3d` holding it that names one, or none.
matte.title: Matte

position.description: Position in world units along X, Y and Z, in the parent's space.
position.title: Position

rotation.description:
Rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z, applied as yaw about Y, then pitch about the turned
X, then roll about the turned Z.
rotation.title: Rotation

scale.description: Scale multiplier along X, Y and Z, applied before the rotation.
scale.title: Scale

visible.description:
Whether the merge and everything wired into it is in the scene. While false, nothing
reached only through it is evaluated, drawn or decoded: objects, lights and cameras
alike.
visible.title: Visible

oneOf.title: Merge 3D

oneOf.description:
A glTF model: the default scene of a `.glb`, with its metallic-roughness materials, vertex
colours, two sets of texture coordinates with `KHR_texture_transform`, skins, morph targets
and animation clips. A raster wired into `texture` shows on the surfaces of the material
`texture_material` names, such as a screen. With a scene wired into `projector` as well, the
texture is projected onto those surfaces from the scene's camera instead, as a `material_3d`'s
`projector` projects its texture, where faces turned away and points out of view show white;
naming the model's only material projects a plate onto all of it. The model's own lights and a
camera are added with `lights` and `camera`. Points, lines, and triangle strips and fans aren't
drawn, with a `scene.model_primitives_skipped` warning.

animation.description:
The animation clip to play, by its name or else its index; empty plays none. A model's
clips are listed in the `animations` of its upload's `metadata` on a host that takes
uploads, and by `modelInfo` in the browser bindings.
animation.title: Animation

animation_loop.description: Plays the clip again from its start once it ends, rather than holding its last pose.
animation_loop.title: Animation Loop

animation_offset.description: Seconds into the clip at the clip's first frame.
animation_offset.title: Animation Offset

camera.description:
The model's camera to view the scene from, by its name or else its index, placed by the
first node that places it, without that node's scale; empty uses none. It counts as a
`camera_3d` at this node, so the first camera in the scene still wins. Its aspect ratio is
the output's. A model's cameras are listed in the `cameras` of its upload's `metadata` on
a host that takes uploads, and by `modelInfo` in the browser bindings.
camera.title: Camera

cast_shadows.description:
Blocks light from lights that cast shadows, in the posed shape and where masked or blended
materials' alpha reaches their cutoff, or half for blended ones. Unlit and glowing
materials block it too, so a model of a lamp around a light needs this off.
cast_shadows.title: Cast Shadows

lights.description:
Adds the model's own `KHR_lights_punctual` lights to the scene, where its nodes place
them, as `light_3d` nodes there would light it: a directional light's intensity, in lux, and
a point or spot light's, in candela, are `light_3d` intensities as they are, so a point
light of intensity `I` lights a surface `d` metres away as a directional one of `I / d²`
does. A spot light's cone fades from its inner angle out to its outer one. They cast no
shadows, and a scene they light gets no default lights.
lights.title: Lights

matte.description:
The matte its visible coverage goes to, by a name `render_3d`'s `mattes` lists, for that
render's `matte` output. Empty takes the matte of the nearest `merge_3d`, `instance_3d` or
`particles_3d` holding it that names one, or none.
matte.title: Matte

position.description: Position in world units along X, Y and Z, in the parent's space.
position.title: Position

projector_occlusion.description:
With a `projector` wired, the surfaces showing `texture` that the projector can't see,
behind surfaces that cast shadows, show white.
projector_occlusion.title: Projector Occlusion

receive_shadows.description: Darkens where shadows fall on its lit surfaces.
receive_shadows.title: Receive Shadows

rotation.description:
Rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z, applied as yaw about Y, then pitch about the turned
X, then roll about the turned Z.
rotation.title: Rotation

scale.description: Scale multiplier along X, Y and Z, applied before the rotation.
scale.title: Scale

source.description:
A binary glTF (`.glb`) file with its buffers and images inside it: a path or `media`
alias, or `asset:<id>` for a model asset of the host's.
source.title: Source

texture_material.description:
The material, by name, whose surfaces show the `texture` input instead, unlit. A model's
materials are listed in the `materials` of its upload's `metadata` on a host that takes
uploads, and by `modelInfo` in the browser bindings.
texture_material.title: Texture Material

oneOf.title: Model 3D

oneOf.description:
Blurs everything that moves in its source, including what analytic motion blur can't see:
animated sizes, path data, motion upstream of a transform and motion inside video. Analytic
motion blur in the source is off while it samples, and so is a `motion_blur` inside it.
Content that already has its own motion blur, like a video recorded with it, is blurred
twice.

samples.description:
Sub-frames rendered across the shutter, from 1 to 64. Each renders the whole source
again, so the cost grows with it. 1 renders the source once, at the frame.
samples.title: Samples

shutter.description:
Shutter angle in degrees, centred on the frame, from 0 to 360. 0 is off, 180 is the
usual film look and 360 smears over the whole frame.
shutter.title: Shutter

oneOf.title: Motion Blur

oneOf.description:
Grows its geometry's outline by `offset`, or shrinks it when negative, rounding the corners
it grows around; chained offsets add up. Fills and strokes of the result follow the offset
outline: a stroke is centred on it, so it lies where the signed distance from the original
outline equals the offset. The offset is taken from the outline the fill covers, so a path's
open contours count as closed by their closing segment, and a stroke of an offset path
strokes that closed outline. Trim and dash on such a stroke are measured along the original
outline and carried across to the offset one, so around a corner the offset rounds, the
stroke keeps the place the corner has.

offset.description:
Distance in the geometry's untransformed pixels that the outline grows outward by, or
shrinks inward by when negative.
offset.title: Offset

oneOf.title: Offset 2D

oneOf.description: Uniformly adjusts raster opacity.

opacity.description: Opacity multiplier applied to the raster.
opacity.title: Opacity

oneOf.title: Opacity

oneOf.description:
Reduces a raster to a few levels with a Bayer threshold matrix, which trades the banding of
plain quantizing for a fixed, regular pattern. Values quantize in sRGB-encoded space. The
matrix is anchored to the canvas origin and each cell is a whole number of device pixels, so
cell edges are never antialiased. The source's alpha is kept.

For example, `{ "matrix": "bayer8", "pitch": 2, "ink": [20, 24, 40, 255], "paper": [240, 232, 210, 255] }`
redraws a photo in two colours with cells of 2 pixels.

ink.description:
Color of the darkest level. Must be a solid color; a gradient is an error. Only
`ink_paper` uses it.
ink.title: Ink

levels.description: Levels each value quantizes to, at least 2. 2 gives only the extremes.
levels.title: Levels

paper.description:
Color of the lightest level. Must be a solid color; a gradient is an error. Only
`ink_paper` uses it.
paper.title: Paper

pitch.description:
Width and height of a matrix cell in pixels. A cell is a whole number of output pixels, at
least one, so the pitch rounds at render scales where it isn't.
pitch.title: Pitch

oneOf.title: Ordered Dither

oneOf.description:
Draws `count` copies of its `object` scene as particles, scattered over its `surface` scene:
each is emitted from a point picked at random over the surface's triangles, as likely
anywhere as anywhere else of the same area, then moves along a direction near the
triangle's normal with `speed` and falls with `gravity`. Without a surface, particles are
emitted from the node's origin along +Y. The surface isn't drawn; wire it into a `merge_3d` as
well to show it. The defaults scatter all the particles at once and keep them still, which
suits grass on a hill or rocks on a floor; a `rate`, `lifetime` and `speed` make it an emitter,
such as sparks or snow.

A frame's particles depend only on the seed, the params, the surface and the time, which is
the frame over the composition's frame rate, so any frame renders alone and the same, and a
`motion_blur` blurs particles by their motion. Particles are placed on the GPU: a frame's CPU
work doesn't grow with `count`, and each `particles_3d` counts once towards a scene's 100000
objects, however many particles it draws.

The surface is taken at rest: a skinned or morphed model emits from its vertices as they are
stored, unposed, and an `instance_3d` in it emits from all its copies. Each object of the
surface emits in proportion to its area in the world, so a flat plane or a flattened box still
emits, and an `image_plane_3d` with a `region` emits from the part it shows. Emit points
follow the surface where it is at the frame. A surface with no area emits nothing.

Particles are drawn as `instance_3d` copies are, sharing the object's meshes and materials,
with its lights and camera left out. They are drawn at once, with no order among them, so the
object must be opaque or masked: a blended surface, or one showing a raster such as an image
plane, fails the render. Fade particles with `scale_over_life` rather than opacity. A
`particles_3d` may sit under an `instance_3d` of `count` 1, which places it as a group would,
but more copies of particles, particles of particles, and particles emitted from particles
fail the render.

align_to_normal.description:
Turns each particle so that its +Y follows the normal of the surface where it was emitted.
Off, particles keep the node's axes.
align_to_normal.title: Align To Normal

count.description:
Particles, from 0 to 100000. Each is one copy of `object`. With `rate` above 0, they are
slots that are born one after another and born again once all have been.
count.title: Count

gravity.description:
Acceleration in world units per second squared along X, Y and Z, in the node's own space:
`[0, -9.8, 0]` makes particles fall. A particle is at `emit + velocity * age + gravity *
age² / 2`.
gravity.title: Gravity

lifetime.description:
Seconds a particle lives once born, after which it draws nothing until it is born again.
0 lives until it is born again, or forever when `rate` is 0. With `rate` above 0, a
particle is born again every `count / rate` seconds, which cuts a longer lifetime short.
lifetime.title: Lifetime

matte.description:
The matte, by a name `render_3d`'s `mattes` lists, of every object inside it that names
none of its own, for that render's `matte` output. Empty passes on the matte of the
nearest `merge_3d`, `instance_3d` or `particles_3d` holding it that names one, or none.
matte.title: Matte

position.description: Position in world units along X, Y and Z of the whole system in the parent's space: the surface, the particles and, without a surface, the point they are emitted from move with it.
position.title: Position

rate.description:
Particles born per second: particle `k` is born `k / rate` seconds into the composition,
and born again, somewhere new, every `count / rate` seconds after. 0 gives birth to all of
them at once, at 0 seconds, and never again.
rate.title: Rate

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z of the whole system, applied as yaw about Y, then pitch about the turned X, then roll about the turned Z. It turns `gravity`, and the direction particles are emitted along without a surface, with the rest.
rotation.title: Rotation

rotation_jitter.description:
Most degrees a particle turns about an axis picked at random, by an angle picked at random
up to this. 180 turns particles every way.
rotation_jitter.title: Rotation Jitter

scale.description:
The smallest and largest uniform scale of a particle, each picked at random between them.
Negative scales are taken as 0.
scale.title: Scale

scale_over_life.description:
The scale multiplier at a particle's birth and at the end of its `lifetime`, between which
it moves in a straight line with its age. Fade particles out with an end of 0. With a
`lifetime` of 0 the start applies throughout.
scale_over_life.title: Scale Over Life

seed.description:
Picks an unrelated scatter: where each particle is emitted, and its direction, size and
turn. The same seed gives the same particles at the same time.
seed.title: Seed

speed.description:
World units per second a particle moves at, along its emit direction, from where it is
emitted.
speed.title: Speed

spread.description:
Degrees the emit direction may lean from the surface normal, or from +Y without a surface,
at random within a cone: 0 emits along the normal and 180 every way.
spread.title: Spread

oneOf.title: Particles 3D

oneOf.description: Produces a rasterized vector path source.

anchor.description: Pivot for scale and rotation, in pixels relative to `position`.
anchor.title: Anchor

feather.description:
Width in untransformed pixels over which the fill's edge fades out, centred on the
edge. 0 keeps a sharp edge.
feather.title: Feather

fill_paint.description: Fill paint. Accepts a solid color or gradient.
fill_paint.title: Fill Paint

motion_blur.description:
Motion blur shutter angle in degrees, centred on the frame. 0 is off, 180 is the
usual film look and 360 smears over the whole frame.
motion_blur.title: Motion Blur

offset.description:
Distance in untransformed pixels that the fill grows outward by, or shrinks inward by
when negative, rounding the corners it grows around. A shape shrunk past its middle
vanishes. The stroke stays on the outline in `data`.
offset.title: Offset

repeat.description: Copies of the path drawn in one pass. Absent draws the path once.
repeat.title: Repeat

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees, about the anchor.
rotation.title: Rotation

scale.description: Scale multiplier per axis, about the anchor.
scale.title: Scale

stroke_dash.description:
Lengths in untransformed pixels that the stroke alternately draws and skips along each
contour, starting with a dash. An odd number of lengths is repeated to make the
pattern, as in SVG. Each dash has round caps, so a dash of length 0 draws a dot. No
lengths, or only zeros, draw a solid stroke. Dashes are measured along the whole
contour, and `trim_start` and `trim_end` then clip them.
stroke_dash.title: Stroke dash

stroke_dash_offset.description:
Distance in untransformed pixels into the dash pattern at which each contour starts.
Increasing it moves the dashes toward the start of the contour.
stroke_dash_offset.title: Stroke dash offset

stroke_paint.description: Stroke paint. Accepts a solid color or gradient.
stroke_paint.title: Stroke Paint

stroke_width.description:
Stroke width in untransformed pixels. Under non-uniform scale the stroke stretches
with the path, so it is wider across the more scaled axis.
stroke_width.title: Stroke Width

trim_end.description: Normalized end of the visible stroke range for each contour.
trim_end.title: Trim end

trim_start.description: Normalized start of the visible stroke range for each contour.
trim_start.title: Trim start

oneOf.title: Path

oneOf.description:
The outline of SVG path data, without paint. The fill covers it under the even-odd rule, and
a stroke follows its contours, leaving the closing segment of an open contour unstroked.
Curves are flattened for the largest scale `render_2d` draws them at.

anchor.description: Pivot for scale and rotation, in pixels relative to `position`.
anchor.title: Anchor

data.description: SVG-style path data, laid out in untransformed pixels from `position`.
data.title: Path data

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees, about the anchor.
rotation.title: Rotation

scale.description: Scale multiplier per axis, about the anchor.
scale.title: Scale

oneOf.title: Path 2D

oneOf.description:
Sorts runs of pixels along rows or columns by brightness, hue or saturation, which smears a
picture into streaks.

Only pixels whose `key` lies from `low` to `high` are sorted. A run is a span of those pixels
along the `direction`; pixels outside the band, and fully transparent ones, stay where they
are and end the run. A run longer than `max_length` is cut into pieces at multiples of
`max_length` pixels from the canvas origin. Each run is sorted from the lowest `key` to the
highest, or the reverse, and pixels with equal keys keep their order. A pixel moves whole, its
alpha with its colour, so the output holds exactly the pixels of the source.

For example, `{ "key": "luma", "low": 0.2, "high": 0.9, "max_length": 120 }` drags the lit
parts of a photo into horizontal streaks up to 120 pixels long.

direction.description: The direction runs of pixels are taken along.
direction.title: Direction

high.description: The highest `key`, 0 to 1, a pixel may have and still be sorted.
high.title: High

key.description: The value that selects pixels and orders them.
key.title: Key

low.description: The lowest `key`, 0 to 1, a pixel may have and still be sorted.
low.title: Low

max_length.description:
The most pixels one run holds, 2 and up. Longer runs are cut at multiples of it from the
canvas origin, and each piece is sorted alone. At most 1024 device pixels: a larger value,
or one that a render scale takes past that, counts as 1024.
max_length.title: Max Length

reverse.description: Sorts from the highest `key` to the lowest instead.
reverse.title: Reverse

oneOf.title: Pixel Sort

oneOf.description:
Reduces a raster to a few colours, either by quantizing each channel to `levels` steps or by
mapping the brightness of each pixel onto the colours of a palette. Both work on the
sRGB-encoded colour, where steps are evenly spaced to the eye, and keep the source's alpha.

In `palette` mode the colours are sorted by their brightness, the Rec. 709 luma of the encoded
colour, and a pixel takes the colour whose band it falls in, the bands splitting at the
midpoints between neighbouring colours. `dither` places the pixels near a boundary in an 8 × 8
Bayer pattern anchored to the canvas origin, so it holds still when the source moves and when
the render scale changes.

For example, `{ "mode": "palette", "colors": [[8, 8, 8, 255], [191, 20, 20, 255], [201, 209, 214, 255]] }`
prints a photo in three inks.

colors.description:
The colours a pixel may take, 2 to 16, as solid sRGB colours. Only `palette` uses it. Their
alpha is ignored.
colors.title: Colors

dither.description:
How much of an 8 × 8 Bayer pattern is added before quantizing, 0 to 1. 0 gives hard bands,
and 1 mixes neighbouring steps or colours in proportion to how far between them a pixel
lies.
dither.title: Dither

levels.description:
Steps each channel quantizes to, 2 to 256. 2 gives only the extremes. Only `levels` uses
it.
levels.title: Levels

mode.description: What the node reduces the colour to.
mode.title: Mode

oneOf.title: Posterize

oneOf.description: Blurs a raster along circles about a centre, as a spin.

amount.description: Arc in degrees each pixel is spread along about `center`, centred on it, up to 360.
amount.title: Amount

center.description:
Centre of the spin in canvas pixels. The canvas centre, `[width / 2, height / 2]`, when
absent.
center.title: Center

edge.description: What the source reads as beyond the canvas.
edge.title: Edge

oneOf.title: Radial Blur

oneOf.description: Composites a variadic stack of raster layers in order.

blend_mode.description:
Blend mode used for each layer in the stack. `normal` composites in linear light; every
other mode applies its formula to the sRGB-encoded colours and composites the result in
linear light.
blend_mode.title: Blend Mode

opacity.description: Opacity of each layer above the first, which is the base and is used as is.
opacity.title: Opacity

oneOf.title: Raster Multi Merge

oneOf.description:
Rasterizes a drawing in one pass over the canvas: each 16 by 16 pixel tile composites the
drawables that reach it, in order, with normal blending. Outlines are measured per pixel, so
they stay sharp under any transform.
oneOf.title: Render 2D

oneOf.description:
Draws a 3D scene into a raster, with a transparent background unless it shows its environment
map; or, by `output`, its depth or normals, for 2D effects such as fog, or the mattes of its
objects. Its `color`, `depth`, `normal` and `matte` outputs read each of them from the one
render.

A matte selects objects after rendering without drawing the scene again: name the lettering
`title` with its `matte` param, list `mattes: ["title"]`, and a `merge` whose `overlay` is the
`color` output, whose `base` is a `blur` of it, and whose `mask` is the `matte` output with
`mask_mode` `red` keeps the title sharp while the rest blurs. A matte's edges are antialiased
with the colour's, by `supersample`, so they line up.

depth_far.description:
Distance from the camera, in world units, that `depth` output maps to 1, and past which it
stays 1. 0 uses the camera's `far`, which spreads the 0 to 1 range thin over a scene much
nearer than it.
depth_far.title: Depth Far

depth_near.description:
Distance from the camera, in world units, that `depth` output maps to 0. 0 uses the
camera's `near`.
depth_near.title: Depth Near

dof_samples.description:
Views through the camera's lens averaged for its depth of field, each a draw of the scene
at the supersampled size: more is a smoother blur. Does nothing while the camera's `f_stop`
is 0 or its projection is orthographic, and at 1. The `depth` and `normal` outputs are
drawn from the centre of the lens, sharp.
dof_samples.title: Dof Samples

environment.description:
Brightness of the light from all around that surfaces reflect and are lit by: the
`environment_map` when one is set, and otherwise a built-in studio of softboxes. 0 turns it
off.
environment.title: Environment

environment_background.description:
Shows the environment map behind the scene, through the exposure and tone mapping but not
the fog, which makes the output opaque. Shadow catchers darken it.
environment_background.title: Environment Background

environment_background_blur.description: How blurred the background is, as a surface of this roughness reflects it: 0 is sharp.
environment_background_blur.title: Environment Background Blur

environment_map.description:
An equirectangular Radiance `.hdr` or OpenEXR `.exr` file that lights the scene from all
around in place of the studio: a path or `media` alias, or `asset:<id>` for an environment
map asset of the host's. Its centre is the view along -Z, with +X to its right and +Y at
its top, and it is stretched over the whole sphere whatever its aspect. Non-finite and
negative pixels are read as black. While a map lights a scene without lights, it gets no

A primitive solid: box, sphere, plane, cylinder, torus or cone, centred on its position. Lit,
single-sided and white unless a `material_3d` is wired into `material`. Its material's
`texture` shows upright seen from outside: whole on each face of a box, the top and bottom
faces upright to a camera on +Z tilted to look at them, and whole on a plane seen from above,
its top edge towards -Z. A sphere, cylinder, cone or torus wraps it around Y, its left edge at
-Z and running towards -X, so a camera on +Z sees its middle. A sphere maps it
equirectangularly from the top pole to the bottom one, and a cylinder's or cone's side from
top to bottom, with the circle inscribed in the texture on each cap, upright as on a box. A
torus wraps the texture's height around its tube, from the inner equator over the top, so its
middle row runs around the outer equator.

`right_material`, `front_material` and `back_material`, which are its +Y, -Y, -X, +X, +Z and
-Z faces in its own axes before `rotation`; the front faces a camera looking down -Z. A face
with none wired uses `material`, and each face shows its own material's texture. A face
material wired into any other shape fails the render naming the input. The faces draw as one
object each, merged where neighbours share a material, from the same mesh, so a box with face
materials costs a draw for each run of faces, and under `instance_3d` each draws all its
copies.

oneOf.description:
Sharpens a raster with an unsharp mask: detail is the difference between a pixel's luminance
and that of a blurred copy, and sharpening adds `amount` times it back.

It works on straight colour, with luminance (Rec. 709) on the sRGB-encoded values. The detail
is `luminance - blurred luminance`, reduced towards 0 by `threshold`, and the sharpened
luminance is `luminance + amount * detail`. That is held between the darkest and brightest
luminance in the 3×3 pixels around it, so hard edges get no light or dark halo. The change is
added equally to red, green and blue, which keeps the hue and adds no colour fringes; colour
brighter than white stays unclipped. Alpha is unchanged and the output covers the source's
area. For example, `amount` 1.5 with `radius` 2 and `threshold` 0.02 firms up edges and fine
texture while leaving faint grain alone.

threshold.description:

detail, such as noise, is left alone, and stronger detail is sharpened by what exceeds it.

oneOf.description:
The outlines of text's glyphs, without paint, so fills, strokes, offsets and shadows style
type as they do any other geometry, and one `text_2d` can feed several of them:

```json
{ "id": 1, "type": "text_2d", "params": { "content": "Lumen", "font_size": 240, "position": [960, 540], "alignment_horizontal": "center", "alignment_vertical": "middle" } },
{ "id": 2, "type": "offset_2d", "params": { "offset": 12 }, "in": { "geometry": 1 } },
{ "id": 3, "type": "fill_2d", "params": { "paint": "#ee5b24" }, "in": { "geometry": 2 } },
{ "id": 4, "type": "fill_2d", "params": { "paint": "#ffffff" }, "in": { "geometry": 1 } },
{ "id": 5, "type": "stroke_2d", "params": { "paint": "#111111", "width": 4 }, "in": { "geometry": 1 } },
{ "id": 6, "type": "merge_2d", "in": { "drawings": [3, 4, 5] } },
{ "id": 7, "type": "render_2d", "in": { "drawing": 6 } }
```

The text is shaped as a `text` node with the same font, size and layout shapes it, with its
kerning, ligatures, font fallback and wrapping, so with left and top alignment a white fill
lines up with a white `text` node at the same `position`. The outline covers what the glyphs
cover by the nonzero rule, as fonts expect, so contours that overlap, as in variable fonts,
and glyphs that overlap each other fill as one, and a stroke follows only the outline's
edge, measuring trim and dash along each of its contours. Glyphs are shaped and outlined
again only when the text, font or layout change, not when the transform or the styles
animate. Text of more than 8192 outline points is drawn as several outlines one after
another, glyph by glyph, which shadows and translucent paints treat as separate drawables
where they overlap. Curves are flattened for the largest scale `render_2d` draws them at,
coarser where a text would pass 1048576 points.

It suits titles and short lines. A moving paragraph costs far more than a `text` node, whose
glyphs are drawn from cached images, since its outline is placed again every frame. One
style covers the whole text: rich text spans, decorations and the `glyph_*` params of a
`text` node have no counterpart.

builtins.doc: Angle in radians of the point `(x, y)` from the +x axis, in `-π..=π`.
builtins.name: atan2

builtins.doc: Maps `value` from `from_min..from_max` onto `to_min..to_max` without clamping. `from_min` and `from_max` must differ.
builtins.name: remap

builtins.doc: Hermite smoothing of `x` between two edges.
builtins.name: smoothstep

builtins.doc: Laid-out height of a string, or of `node(id)` for a text node.
builtins.name: text_height

builtins.doc: Laid-out width of a string, or of `node(id)` for a text node.
builtins.name: text_width

builtins.doc: A number as text with exactly `decimals` digits after the point (default 0), so `format(4.3, 2)` is `'4.30'`. Halves round away from zero on the number as written: `format(2.5)` is `'3'`, `format(-2.5)` is `'-3'` and `format(1.005, 2)` is `'1.01'`. A result shorter than `width` characters (default 0) is padded on the left with `fill`, one Unicode code point (default a space); with a `'0'` fill the sign stays first, so `format(-5, 0, 4, '0')` is `'-005'`. `value` must be finite, `decimals` a whole number in `0..=20` and `width` a whole number in `0..=64`.
builtins.name: format

builtins.doc: Joins strings and numbers into one string. A number shows as it does in a text param, so `concat('frame ', frame / 7)` reads like `=frame / 7`; use `format` for a fixed number of decimals or padding, e.g. `concat('frame ', format(frame, 0, 4, '0'), ' / 1200')`. `+` stays numeric. The result can be at most 1 MiB.
builtins.name: concat

builtins.doc: Colour from components in `0..=255`, alpha included.
builtins.name: rgba

builtins.doc: 0 before frame `start`, 1 after frame `end`, linear in between.
builtins.name: progress

builtins.doc: Eases from `from` to `to` over `duration` frames from frame `start`. `ease` defaults to `'linear'`.
builtins.name: tween

builtins.doc: Applies an easing to progress `t`, e.g. `ease('out_expo', progress(0, 18))`.
builtins.name: ease

builtins.doc: The easing CSS writes `cubic-bezier(out.x, out.y, in.x, in.y)`. Both x components must be in `0..=1`.
builtins.name: cubic_bezier

builtins.doc: A keyframe for `keyframes`: `value` at `at`, a number, vec2, vec3, colour, path data or text. `ease` is how the curve leaves this key toward the next. Text that isn't path data can't interpolate, so a key holding it needs the `'hold'` easing. The `'smooth'` easing passes through every key with continuous speed, taking each key's slope from its neighbours; it doesn't overshoot, and applies to numbers, vectors and colours.
builtins.name: key

builtins.doc: The value of keys ordered by `at` at time `t`, usually `frame`. `ease` may be left out; it is the easing of keys without one and defaults to `'linear'`. Before the first key and after the last, the value holds. Keys at the same `at` jump. With `'smooth'`, the curve is a cubic Hermite spline through the keys: it has continuous speed at every key, takes the slope at a key from the keys either side (one-sided next to an end, a jump or a key with another easing), and is limited per component so it doesn't overshoot between keys.
builtins.name: keyframes

builtins.doc: The value of a composition template's prop, e.g. `prop('title')`. Only inside a template.
builtins.name: prop

builtins.doc: Smooth gradient noise in `-1..=1`, continuous in `x` and varying about once per unit. Each `seed` is an unrelated curve. Arguments must be finite.
builtins.name: noise

builtins.doc: Uniform number in `0..1`, fixed by its inputs. `random(x)` is `random(seed, x)` with seed 0; e.g. `random(glyph)`. Arguments must be finite.
builtins.name: random

builtins.doc: Spring from 0 to 1, `t` seconds after release, e.g. `spring((frame - 12) / fps)`. Stiffness defaults to 170 and damping to 26.
builtins.name: spring

builtins.doc: The point `t` of the way along path data by arc length, so that `t` moving steadily moves the point at a steady speed. `t` is clamped to `0..=1`. Moves between contours add no length, and a closed contour's closing segment does.
builtins.name: path_point

builtins.doc: The direction in degrees that path data heads at `path_point(path_data, t)`, clockwise from +x like `rotation`. It counts whole turns along the path instead of wrapping, so a clockwise circle ends at 360.
builtins.name: path_angle

builtins.doc: Ease-in-out that pulls back and overshoots.
builtins.name: in_out_back

builtins.doc: Ease-in that oscillates like a spring.
builtins.name: in_elastic

builtins.doc: Ease-out that overshoots and oscillates like a spring.
builtins.name: out_elastic

builtins.doc: Ease-in-out that oscillates at both ends.
builtins.name: in_out_elastic

builtins.doc: Ease-out that bounces like a dropped ball.
builtins.name: out_bounce

builtins.doc: Ease-in-out that bounces at both ends.
builtins.name: in_out_bounce

forms.doc: `then` when `condition` is truthy, otherwise `else`. Only the chosen branch is evaluated.
forms.name: if

forms.doc: The value of another node's param. `node(id)` alone names a text node for `text_width` and `text_height`.
forms.name: node

globals.name: glyph

globals.doc: Index of the word being drawn. Only in a text node's `glyph_*` params.
globals.name: word

globals.doc: Index of the line being drawn. Only in a text node's `glyph_*` params.
globals.name: line

globals.doc: Index of the span being drawn, or 0 in plain text. Only in a text node's `glyph_*` params.
globals.name: span

globals.doc: Number of glyphs in the text. Only in a text node's `glyph_*` params.
globals.name: glyph_count

globals.doc: Number of words in the text. Only in a text node's `glyph_*` params.
globals.name: word_count

globals.doc: Number of lines in the text. Only in a text node's `glyph_*` params.
globals.name: line_count

globals.doc: Number of spans in the text, or 1 in plain text. Only in a text node's `glyph_*` params.
globals.name: span_count

globals.doc: Index of the copy being placed, from 0. Only in an `instance_3d`'s `position`, `rotation`, `scale` and `tint` params.
globals.name: instance

globals.doc: Number of copies. Only in an `instance_3d`'s `position`, `rotation`, `scale` and `tint` params.
